title: Plan Part 2
eyebrow: Proposal · adds to the combined plan · nothing built yet

short.lead: You asked for five more things on top of the combined plan, which stays as the base. First, picking a priority is needed to add any task, and setting a due date takes one tap. Second, 'Needs review' ranks above 'In progress'. Third, phone and desktop share one carousel (a row of cards you slide sideways). Desktop shows five cards at once, and you can move along it with the arrow keys or a mouse. Fourth, a Tidy up step closes what no longer needs to exist, and a Triage step then ranks what is left. Fifth, a Roadmap shows where you are and how far you have come, and it updates as you finish or add tasks. The pictures below are drawings, not the built app. Numbers marked 'example' are made up to fill the drawing.
short.hint: Tap each row to see its picture. Start with 'The two loops', which shows how the new screens connect to the ones from the combined plan.
items: The top row is every day: add a task, open Start here, use Focus, tick it off. The bottom row is for when the list feels too big, maybe once a week: Tidy up, then Triage, then Roadmap. Triage decides which three tasks Start here suggests. Each task you tick off moves the Roadmap forward.
Follow the top row, then the bottom row.

items.alt: Two rows of boxes. Top: Add a task, Start here, Focus, Done. Bottom: Tidy up, Triage, Roadmap. Triage points up to Start here; Done points down to Roadmap.
items.caption: The daily loop and the weekly loop. A drawing, not built.

items: Priority needed, due date one tap

After you type a task and press Add, a panel slides up. Priority has four buttons: Urgent (today), High (this week), Medium (soon) and Low (some day). Due date has Today, Tomorrow, Friday, Next week, Pick a date and None. The big button repeats what you chose, for example 'Add to Health · High · due Friday'.
Check that the four priority words and their hints match how you think about urgency.

items.caption: Adding a task on a phone. A drawing, not built.

items: Until you tap a priority, the big button is greyed out and reads 'Pick a priority to add'. Due date is optional and starts on None. Today the app lets a task be saved with no priority at all.

items: The jotter, project cards, the Board and Sort all use this one row. Keys 1 to 4 pick the priority, and you can type a date such as 'fri' or '15 dec'. Enter adds the task. On any card, the priority and due date are small chips you tap to change.
Check that the chips on the card under the row are easy to spot.

items: Same carousel as the phone, five at a time

Desktop stops laying out every card on one long page. It shows the same project and kind-of-work carousels as the phone, five cards at a time. The left and right arrow keys move along, Enter picks, and typing a name jumps to that project. A mouse wheel or trackpad swipe sideways also moves the row.
Compare it with 'Focus, desktop' in the combined plan.

items: The phone shows one and a half cards, so you can see there is more to the right. 'Find a project' sits above the folders. The bottom menu gets a fifth tab, Plan, which holds Tidy up, Triage and Roadmap.

items: Step 1: does each task still need to exist?

The app groups tasks and issues that look finished, repeated or forgotten, and says why each group is there. 'Built, waiting for your review' (15) means a finished change on GitHub already mentions it. 'Replaced by newer work' (8) covers the old issues about the Board. 'Looks the same as another' finds pairs like issue #154 and issue #236, which are both about the mobile icon. 'Not touched in 60 days' asks if you still want it. You press Keep or Close on each. Nothing closes on GitHub until you press Confirm. The 15, the 8 and the pair of issues #154 and #236 are real. The 4 beside 'Looks the same' and the 21 beside the 60-day group are examples.
Check that the four groups are the right reasons to close something.

items.alt: Desktop drawing: Tidy up with four groups of issues, Keep and Close buttons, and a side panel showing 97 to 67 open with a Confirm 30 and go to Triage button
items.caption: Tidy up on desktop. A drawing, not built.

items: What is left gets ranked into Now, Next and Later. The rules are on the right, in order: needs review, in progress, past its date or due today, priority, blocks other tasks from starting, due soonest, oldest. 'Needs review' comes first, above 'In progress', as you asked. Today the app does not know 'Needs review' at all; it is only a GitHub label, so the app would learn to read it. You can drag a task to change the order, and your order wins. The Now list is what Start here suggests.
Check the order of the seven rules.

items.alt: Desktop drawing: Triage with Now, Next and Later lists, and seven numbered rules on the right starting with Needs review then In progress
items.caption: Triage on desktop. A drawing, not built.

items: Each project gets a row, and each block is a group of tasks (a parent task with its subtasks, or a GitHub milestone, which is a named goal that holds a set of issues) with its own progress bar. Blocks sit in Now, Next or Later from Triage. The big number at the top shows how much of your open work is done since the last time you finished Tidy up. All the numbers in this picture are examples.
Check that one row per project is how you want to see it.

items: On a phone the Roadmap is one list: Now, then Next, with Later folded away. The three steps sit at the top as tabs, so you can go back to Tidy up or Triage.

items.alt: Phone drawing: Tidy, Triage and Roadmap tabs, 41 percent, Now and Next blocks with progress bars, Later folded, and the Plan tab selected

choices: jot
Does a quick thought in the jotter need a priority too?
No, it gets one when you sort it
Jotting stays one step. Sort asks for the priority before the thought becomes a task.
Yes, every time
Nothing is ever saved without a priority, but jotting gains a step.
I suggest 1 because the jotter exists to catch a thought before it slips, and Sort already asks you about each one.
nav
Where do Tidy up, Triage and Roadmap go on a phone?
A fifth tab called Plan
One tap from anywhere, as in the pictures. The tabs are Start, Focus, Sort, Board, Plan.
Inside Projects
Projects keeps its tab, and the three steps are a button at its top.
I suggest 1 because the weekly loop is a habit, and a habit is easier with its own tab.
order
How should I build it, together with the combined plan?
Priority and needs review first
Then Start here, then the shared carousel, then Tidy up, Triage and Roadmap. Each part makes the next one's ranking trustworthy.
Tidy up, Triage and Roadmap first
You get the backlog clean-up soonest, but the ranking leans on priorities many tasks don't have yet.
I suggest 1 because Triage and Start here rank by priority, so every task needs one first.

wrapup.summary: Part 2 adds a required priority and one-tap due dates, ranks Needs review first, gives phone and desktop one carousel, and adds Tidy up, Triage and Roadmap as a weekly loop. The combined plan stays as the base.
wrapup.changing: Changed: adding a task, task cards, Focus on desktop and the menu. Added: Tidy up, Triage, Roadmap, and the app reading 'Needs review'. Kept: everything else in the combined plan, your data and sync.
wrapup.blocking: Waiting on your answers to the three questions in Choices here and the three on the combined plan page. Nothing is built until you approve.
wrapup.next: After you answer, I will open GitHub issues for each part and build the first one. You get a test page for each part before the next starts.
